content.overview: Section 47 sets out voting rights on poll: every member of a company limited by shares holding equity shares has a right to vote on every resolution, with voting power proportional to paid-up equity capital. Preference shareholders generally vote only on resolutions that affect rights attached to preference shares, winding-up, or reduction of share capital, with specified exceptions when dividends are in arrears.
content.glance: Equity holders vote on every resolution proportionate to paid-up equity; preference holders vote mainly on rights-affecting, winding-up and capital-reduction resolutions; arrears of dividend can enlarge preference voting.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 47 (Voting rights). Subject to section 43 and section 50(2), every member of a company limited by shares holding equity share capital may vote on every resolution placed before the company; on a poll, voting power is in proportion to paid-up equity share capital. A preference shareholder may vote only on resolutions directly affecting the rights attached to the preference shares, on winding up, or on repayment/reduction of share capital. If dividend on a class of preference shares has remained unpaid for two years or more, holders of that class may vote on all resolutions as provided by the section. Apply the rights attached to the relevant share class and the statutory exceptions; do not confuse voting rights with variation of class rights under section 48 or proportional dividend under section 51.

sections.heading: Equity-share voting
sections.body: Subject to section 43 and section 50(2), members holding equity share capital may vote on every resolution. On a poll, voting power is proportional to paid-up equity share capital.

sections.heading: Preference-share voting
sections.body: Preference shareholders generally vote only on resolutions directly affecting rights attached to their preference shares, winding up, or repayment/reduction of share capital.

sections.heading: Dividend arrears
sections.body: Where dividend on a class of preference shares has remained unpaid for two years or more, holders of that class may vote on all resolutions as provided by section 47.

sections.heading: Related provisions
sections.body: Section 48 governs variation of class rights; section 51 concerns proportional dividend where authorised by articles. Neither should be substituted for the voting rules in section 47.

examples.title: Equity poll
examples.body: On a poll, an equity holder with twice the paid-up equity capital of another has twice the voting power under s. 47.

examples.title: Preference on rights variation
examples.body: A resolution altering preference dividend rights triggers preference shareholders’ right to vote under s. 47.

hypotheticals.question: A preference-share class has not received dividends for two years. What voting issue arises?
hypotheticals.analysis: The two-year arrears condition may give holders of that class voting rights on all resolutions under section 47; confirm the arrears period and class-specific facts.

hypotheticals.question: How are equity voting rights calculated on a poll?
hypotheticals.analysis: Voting power is proportional to paid-up equity share capital, subject to the Act and relevant class rights.

distinctions.title: Voting rights and variation of class rights
distinctions.right: Section 48 sets the procedure to vary rights attached to a class.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming preference shareholders can vote on every resolution at all times.
misconceptions.correction: Preference voting is generally limited to specified matters, subject to the two-year dividend-arrears rule.

misconceptions.trap: Calculating poll voting power solely by nominal share count.
misconceptions.correction: For equity shares, poll voting power is proportional to paid-up equity share capital.

misconceptions.trap: Treating a class-rights variation procedure as the voting-rights rule.
misconceptions.correction: Section 47 governs voting; section 48 governs variation of class rights.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When do preference shareholders gain voting rights on all resolutions?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Where dividend on the relevant class of preference shares has remained unpaid for two years or more, subject to section 47.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is equity voting power measured on a poll?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: In proportion to paid-up equity share capital.
